edge_explainer: The de-rate is real and largely mechanical (57x -> 23.4x forward while EPS went $11.31 -> a guided $13.08), and the franchise is unimpaired: 86.7% recurring revenue, record SaaS and total bookings, SaaS +21.7% for a 22nd straight quarter above 20%, FCF +34.7%, and management retiring 5.6% of the shares year-to-date at ~$310 while calling them undervalued. Three things hold this to a 4. FIRST, the growth rate genuinely reset: ARR growth 10.9% -> 10.4% -> 8.2% in two quarters, and the 8.2% INCLUDES For The Record (closed 2026-04-14, $212.7M); at a 4-6x ARR purchase multiple that is $35-53M of acquired ARR, putting ORGANIC ARR growth at roughly 5.8-6.6%. Tyler does not disclose organic ARR and it cannot be derived from any filing - UNVERIFIABLE, and it is the decisive number. SECOND, Q2's GAAP headline is carried by items that are not operations: 'GAAP net income $93.5M, or $2.23 per diluted share, up 10.5%' is true but incomplete - the same income statement carries a $25.048M one-time 'gain on remeasurement of equity investment' ($0 in Q2-25); strip it and GAAP EPS is ~$1.78, DOWN ~12%. GAAP operating income was $95.095M vs $95.596M, DOWN 0.5%, and the release printed operating income WITHOUT a growth rate while giving one for every other metric including, one quarter earlier, operating income itself (+11.9%). THIRD, the guidance raise is financed below the operating line: revenue guidance has not moved since April, while the +$0.45 EPS raise decomposes into +$11M of net interest income from the May convertible proceeds (~+$0.20/sh after tax) and a share count down from February's assumed 44.0M to 40,952,274 (~+$0.50). Emphasis divergence, not fabrication - REVIEW_FLAG, not ELEVATE - but it is why the two-day post-print pop round-tripped. TWO MODE-B FINDINGS CUT THE OTHER WAY. (a) The GWRE analogy is REFUTED: TYL is domestic-only so there is no FX/basis artifact, and maintenance is only $105.8M of $645.1M guided -5 to -7%, a ~1pt drag - the cloud transition is ~87% spent, so the 8.2% has no rev-rec cushion under it and is approximately the true growth rate. (b) The state/local budget fear is NOT the operative risk, and this is where the house has an edge: Tyler's clients are funded by ad-valorem property tax, which is assessed on a LAGGED roll and protected by assessment caps and budget-set levies - aggregate property-tax collections have not fallen y/y in any post-war US recession including 2008-2011; federal exposure is de minimis, so the DOGE channel barely touches Tyler. The fiscal channel that DOES fit the timing is one nobody names: ARPA's $350bn to state and local governments, obligation deadline Dec-2024 and spend deadline Dec-2026, funded exactly this kind of one-time IT modernisation and is now running off - a dated, mechanical explanation for ARR stepping from ~11% to ~8% while budgets themselves stay healthy. HYPOTHESIS, not verified: Tyler does not disclose ARPA-funded revenue. AI-BREAK CONFLICT, stated not averaged: the queue flags ai_complex=false, right about the revenue and wrong about the de-rate - two of the four drawdown legs (2026-01-29, 2026-02-03) were the market pricing AI as a THREAT to vertical software. The entry does NOT require the AI-capex cycle to hold; part of the de-rate is the market's fear that it SUCCEEDS. Against the frozen AI-BREAK|2027-12-31 p=0.45 call and a household already ~$5.2M/26% AI-complex, TYL is one of the few tier-1 names here that leans the other way, and that is the strongest single portfolio reason to own it. CAP STRUCTURE, pulled before any valuation claim: 40,952,274 shares (10-Q cover 2026-07-27) x $305.54 = $12.51bn, matching the queue's $12,513M exactly; cash $895.4M + ST investments $74.7M = $970.0M against $1,408.7M of 0.50% converts due 2031 (capped calls lift the effective conversion price to $655.77, so no dilution at $305) = NET DEBT of $438.6M and EV $12.95bn. There is no net cash here. That gives 23.4x forward non-GAAP EPS, ~35x GAAP, 18.8x EV/FCF, 5.78x EV/ARR, Rule of 40 = 35. SBC is $43.7M in Q2 = 6.8% of revenue and ~25% of guided FCF - a real cost, but buybacks run >5x that, so net dilution is negative. Street's LOWEST target is $395-400 (Stifel, BTIG); my base of $355 is 11% below the Street's floor, flagged rather than hidden because being systematically ~13% low is a documented failure mode of this desk. Verdict: fairly-to-slightly-cheaply priced monopoly, bounded downside (bear FV only -7% from spot), shrinking share count, negative correlation to the book's largest concentrated risk. Ownable small at a price gate. Carry and diversification, not alpha.
